# DoD SRG Impact Level 2 (`dod-il2`)

DoD Cloud Computing Security Requirements Guide level for public / non-controlled unclassified DoD information.

## Customer responsibilities

### Customer-prerequisite and process rules (20)

| Rule | Disposition | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `access-keys-rotated` | customer-prerequisite | IAM user access keys; the enclave creates no IAM users (roles only). Landing-zone identity baseline (IAM Identity Center). |
| `account-part-of-organizations` | customer-prerequisite | The enclave account must be an Organizations member (required for the SCP/RCP layer). Landing zone. |
| `iam-group-has-users-check` | customer-prerequisite | IAM groups/users are not created by the enclave; identity via IAM Identity Center. |
| `iam-root-access-key-check` | customer-prerequisite | Root user hygiene is an account baseline (Control Tower / LZA). |
| `iam-user-group-membership-check` | customer-prerequisite | No IAM users in the enclave; identity via IAM Identity Center. |
| `iam-user-mfa-enabled` | customer-prerequisite | No IAM users in the enclave; identity via IAM Identity Center (MFA enforced there). |
| `iam-user-no-policies-check` | customer-prerequisite | No IAM users in the enclave. |
| `iam-user-unused-credentials-check` | customer-prerequisite | No IAM users in the enclave. |
| `internet-gateway-authorized-vpc-only` | customer-prerequisite | The enclave VPC is customer-supplied and must have no IGW (examples/sandbox-network has none). |
| `mfa-enabled-for-iam-console-access` | customer-prerequisite | No IAM users in the enclave; console access via IAM Identity Center with MFA. |
| `no-unrestricted-route-to-igw` | customer-prerequisite | Customer VPC routing; the enclave requires private subnets without IGW routes. |
| `response-plan-tested` | process | Manual control: incident-response plan exercise. |
| `restricted-common-ports` | customer-prerequisite | Security groups are customer inputs; the sandbox fixture allows only 443/5432 inside the VPC CIDR. |
| `restricted-ssh` | customer-prerequisite | Security groups are customer inputs (endpoint / agent / Aurora SGs); the sandbox fixture opens no SSH. |
| `root-account-hardware-mfa-enabled` | customer-prerequisite | Root user MFA is an account baseline (Control Tower / LZA); cannot be set by IaC. |
| `root-account-mfa-enabled` | customer-prerequisite | Root user MFA is an account baseline; cannot be set by IaC. |
| `subnet-auto-assign-public-ip-disabled` | customer-prerequisite | Customer VPC subnets; the enclave requires private subnets (sandbox fixture complies). |
| `vpc-sg-open-only-to-authorized-ports` | customer-prerequisite | Security groups are customer inputs; no 0.0.0.0/0 ingress in the sandbox fixture. |
| `vpc-vpn-2-tunnels-up` | customer-prerequisite | Site-to-site VPN (e.g. DoD BCAP path) is customer network; the enclave creates none. |
| `vuln-management-plan-exists` | process | Manual control: vulnerability-management plan. |

### Tenant, runtime-only and open-gap rules (5)

| Rule | Disposition | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `elasticache-redis-cluster-automatic-backup-check` | tenant | ElastiCache is allowed for tenants; the enclave creates no cache. |
| `guardduty-non-archived-findings` | runtime-only | Operational: GuardDuty findings must be triaged within the window; the enclave enables GuardDuty (security-services). |
| `rds-snapshots-public-prohibited` | runtime-only | Snapshots exist only at runtime; Aurora is private, and the snapshot-sharing block is set account-wide (see ebs-snapshot-public-restorable-check for EBS). |
| `s3-bucket-policy-grantee-check` | runtime-only | Pack leaves the allowed grantees unset (customer-specific); enclave bucket policies grant only AWS services / the account, with conditions (checked by s3-bucket-ssl-requests-only and PAB mappings). |
| `secretsmanager-scheduled-rotation-success-check` | runtime-only | Rotation outcome is only observable live; the Aurora admin secret is RDS-managed with rotation on. |

### Documented exceptions that apply (12)

| Rule | Resource | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `s3-bucket-default-lock-enabled` | `sgea-<env>-config-*` | AWS Config delivery bucket: S3 rejects writes to Object Lock buckets without a checksum header and the AWS Config writer sends none (verified: InsufficientDeliveryPolicyException). Otherwise identical hardening. |
| `s3-bucket-default-lock-enabled` | `sgea-<env>-access-logs-*` | S3 server-access-log target: log delivery does not support Object Lock targets reliably; access logs are not the system of record. |
| `s3-bucket-replication-enabled` | `sgea-<env>-config-*` | AWS Config retains configuration history itself; the delivery bucket is not replicated. |
| `s3-bucket-replication-enabled` | `sgea-<env>-access-logs-*` | Access-log sink (and its replica-region twin) is not replicated: it records access to the replicated log store. |
| `s3-bucket-replication-enabled` | `sgea-<env>-logs-replica-*` | Cross-region replica of the log store: it is the replication destination. |
| `s3-bucket-logging-enabled` | `sgea-<env>-access-logs-*` | S3 server-access-log target cannot log to itself. |
| `s3-bucket-policy-grantee-check` | `sgea-<env>-config-*` | Config delivery statement grants Principal * restricted by aws:PrincipalArn = the AWS Config service-linked role and the account (AWS's documented pattern for SLR delivery); the rule only matches literal principals. |
| `s3-default-encryption-kms` | `sgea-<env>-access-logs-*` | S3 server-access logging supports only SSE-S3 (AES256) destination buckets, not SSE-KMS (AWS S3 User Guide); the access-log sink uses SSE-S3 with versioning, TLS-only policy and Block Public Access. |
| `lambda-inside-vpc` | `*` (cdk-deploy-helper) | CDK deploy helpers call AWS control-plane APIs during deployment only; they handle no enclave data. |
| `lambda-dlq-check` | `*` (cdk-deploy-helper) | CDK deploy helpers are invoked synchronously by CloudFormation; failures surface as stack events, not dead letters. |
| `cloudtrail-s3-dataevents-enabled` | `*` | The enclave trail records S3 data events for every bucket except its own log store (resources.ARN NotStartsWith the log store): logging the trail's destination would record the trail's own writes in a feedback loop. Object-level access to the log store is recorded by its S3 server access logs (access-log sink), and the store is Object Lock / versioned, CMK-encrypted, replicated. |
| `dynamodb-in-backup-plan` | `*` | Time-dependent: AWS Config can evaluate the new token-ledger table before the backup plan that selects it exists ('No backup plans are available for evaluation'); the periodic re-evaluation (24 h), or start-config-rules-evaluation after deploy (MANUAL-STEPS), turns it COMPLIANT. |
